source_name: CDC Tracking C. auris, National Clinical Cases Reported Over Time
case_definition: Reported U.S. clinical cases of Candida auris by year; not deaths, total prevalence, screening-only cases or necessarily invasive infections
method: Keep 2026-11-13 CDC chart revision as a distinct immutable observed snapshot. Previous CDC 2016–2024 snapshot is never silently overwritten. Revised annual data are NOT NNDSS provisional current-year notification values.
provenance_notes: The CDC website's dated Nov 13, 2026 page includes 2025 annual case totals and changed some historical yearly counts.
The dated latest CDC page is authoritative for that page version; archived old file reflects an earlier CDC tracking page snapshot.
There is a separately defined corrected 2026 MMWR analytical series, not interchangeable with the tracking page.
2026 NNDSS week-by-week notifications are provisional, different in scope, definition and temporal basis.
The observed increased count does not prove a newly discovered pathogen, a local outbreak, or an individual's risk.

context.claim: Candida auris is a newly discovered fungus in 2026
context.evidence: CDC November 11, 2016 described U.S. cases and global reports from 2009–2015.

context.claim: Drug-resistant Candida auris is a documented healthcare-associated hazard
context.evidence: CDC documents antifungal resistance, spread in healthcare facilities and greater risk in already very ill patients.

context.claim: The November 13, 2026 CDC tracking update includes new 2025 annual data and historical revisions
context.evidence: National chart reports 8,780 clinical cases in 2025 and 6,370 in 2024, with revised earlier-year figures.
